title: Magnolia
events_chronological: A prologue recounts three freak coincidences, ending with a boy who jumps from a roof and is killed on the way down by his own mother's shotgun.
Television producer Earl Partridge walked out on his dying wife and their son Jack, who reinvented himself as the seduction guru Frank T.J. Mackey.
Jimmy Gator, host of the quiz show "What Do Kids Know?", abused his daughter Claudia, who has not spoken to him in years.
Donnie Smith was a famous quiz-show child star whose parents kept every cent of his winnings.
Earl Partridge, dying of cancer, is nursed at home by Phil Parma while his young wife Linda comes apart.
Jimmy Gator learns he has months to live and tells his wife Rose that he cannot go on.
Quiz kid Stanley Spector is driven to another taping by a father living off him.
Claudia takes cocaine alone with the stereo at full volume, and a neighbour calls the police.
Officer Jim Kurring answers the call, is charmed by Claudia and asks her out, then loses his gun on a later call and spends the day hunting for it.
Frank Mackey works a hall of men through his "Seduce and Destroy" seminar and is then ambushed in an interview about the father he claims is dead.
Linda goes from lawyer to pharmacy in a rage, trying to have Earl's will changed so that she gets nothing.
Phil tracks Frank down by telephone and begs him to come and see his dying father.
Donnie, in love with a bartender, decides to steal from the office that has just sacked him.
Stanley wets himself on air and refuses to answer another question, and the show collapses live.
Jimmy breaks down on camera and afterwards admits to Rose that he did what Claudia says he did.
Linda swallows her pills in the car and is found by Dixon, a neighbourhood boy who takes her money before calling for help.
Frank arrives at his father's bedside and screams at the unconscious man, then weeps over him.
Jimmy raises a gun to his own head just as frogs begin falling out of the sky over the Valley.
The rain of frogs wrecks cars across the Valley and knocks Donnie off the pole he is climbing, and Kurring picks him up and lets him put the money back.
Earl dies, Linda is taken to hospital, Stanley tells his father to be nicer to him, and Claudia turns to Kurring and smiles.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a self-contained prologue set decades earlier, and everything after it covers a single day in the San Fernando Valley, cut between nine storylines almost continuously. The nonlinearity is less a shuffled timeline than the late release of buried history: told-order bullets 4, 9 and 14 reach years behind the day the film is otherwise living in, and each arrives at the moment it does most damage.
fabula_notes: The nine strands run simultaneously through one day, so a single chronology has to impose an order on scenes the film shows as concurrent. Earl's abandonment of his first family and Jimmy's abuse of Claudia are established through confession and archive footage rather than dramatised as they happened.
